# Corrected Source Map: GOV-003 — Fourth-quarter 2022 Public Finances and Debt

**Document type:** Executive-official financial report (Comunicado No. 9)
**Source role:** Executive_official_report — Ministry of Finance self-presentation
**Reporting period:** Full year 2022 (FY2022), published 30 January 2023
**Institutional scope:** Federal Government / Sector Público (boundaries not explicitly defined in extract)
**Currency basis:** Mexican pesos (MXN); USD used for some international comparisons and debt metrics
**Figures:** Mix of actual results and, for 2023 projections, forward-looking. Preliminary vs. audited status not distinguished in extract.

---

## §1 — Debt Stock and Debt Ratio

| Claim | Locator | Category | Verification |
|---|---|---|---|
| Public debt was **49.4% of GDP** at end-2022 | Block 1, ¶4 | Observed fact (self-reported) | ✅ SUPPORTED — "La deuda pública se ubican en 49.4% del PIB" |
| Debt ratio was **1.6 pp of GDP below** what was budgeted for 2022 | Block 1, ¶4 | Official assertion — comparison basis not stated (nominal vs real, which budget revision?) | ✅ SUPPORTED — "en 1.6 y 1.4 puntos porcentuales del PIB, respectivamente" |
| Debt ratio was **1.4 pp of GDP below** the 2021 level | Block 1, ¶4 | Official assertion — FX-driven or real? Not qualified | ✅ SUPPORTED |
| "Debt is sustainable and lower than 2021" | **Block 5, ¶20** *(correction: draft said Block 5, ¶14)* | Official characterization — no sustainability metric cited | ✅ SUPPORTED at corrected locator — "la deuda pública se sitúan en un nivel sostenible y menor al observado en 2021" |
| Mexico received **21 international recognitions** for debt management strategy over four years | Block 6, ¶19 | Official assertion — unnamed recognitions, no independent verification offered | ✅ SUPPORTED — "México ha recibido 21 reconocimientos internacionales por la estrategia del manejo de deuda" |
| Mexico maintains **investment grade and stable outlook** from all **8 rating agencies** | Block 6, ¶20 | Official assertion — not cross-checked in extract against specific agency statements | ✅ SUPPORTED — "mantiene el grado de inversión y una perspectiva estable de parte de las 8 calificadoras" |
| For 2023 and the next two years, **debt pressures reduced by an average of 73%** due to buyback operations | Block 6, ¶18 | Official assertion — 73% reduction in what metric (refinancing need? debt service?) not specified | ✅ SUPPORTED — "las presiones de deuda se redujeron en promedio 73%" |
| Operations released **3 billion dollars** for the next administration | Block 6, ¶18 | Official assertion — exact definition of "released" not given | ✅ SUPPORTED — "liberaron recursos por 3 mil millones de dólares para la siguiente administración" |

| Claim | Locator | Category | Verification |
|---|---|---|---|

| Revenues were **MXN 422 billion above** the programmed level | Block 4, ¶9 | Official assertion — program = approved budget? Which revision? | ✅ SUPPORTED — "ubicándose 422 mil millones de pesos por encima del programa" |
| Revenues grew **2.5% real YoY** vs 2021; **two consecutive years of growth** | Block 4, ¶9 | Official assertion — 2021 base may include pandemic distortion | ✅ SUPPORTED — "aumentaron en 2.5%... ligaron dos años de crecimientos consecutivos" |
| Federal Government obtained **additional revenues above program of MXN 632 billion**, of which **MXN 397 billion** was the reduced IEPS (fuel tax) subsidy foregone | Block 4, ¶10 | Official assertion — subsidy reduction treated as revenue gain; distributional implications not addressed | ✅ SUPPORTED — "632 mil millones de pesos, de los cuales 397 mil millones de pesos correspondieron a la menor recaudación por el estímulo al IEPS" |
| Oil revenues: **MXN 1,482.2 billion (5.2% of GDP)** — highest since 2014 | Block 4, ¶11 | Observed fact; commodity-price-dependent | ✅ SUPPORTED — "1 billón 482 mil millones de pesos, equivalente a 5.2% del PIB, el nivel más alto observado desde 2014" |
| Oil revenues grew **18.7% real YoY** | Block 4, ¶11 | Official assertion — driven by high oil prices; sustainability not addressed | ✅ SUPPORTED — "incremento real anual de 18.7%" |
| Tax revenues (excluding fuel IEPS): **13.6% of GDP** — highest on record | Block 4, ¶12 | Official assertion — scope (federal only vs. consolidated?) unspecified | ✅ SUPPORTED — "llegaron a 13.6% del PIB. Este es el mayor nivel desde que se tiene registro" |
| Tax revenue grew **7.8% real YoY** — highest since 2016 | Block 4, ¶12 | Official assertion | ✅ SUPPORTED — "aumentó en un 7.8% real anual, la mayor tasa desde 2016" |
| Combatting tax evasion credited for revenue gains, **without new or increased taxes** | Block 4, ¶12 | Official assertion — no independent methodology cited | ✅ SUPPORTED — "El combate a la evasión fiscal continúa reflejándose positivamente... sin aumentar o crear impuestos nuevos" |
| ISR (income tax) reached **MXN 2,270 billion (8.0% of GDP)** — all-time high | Block 4, ¶13 | Observed fact; real-wage-growth linkage asserted | ✅ SUPPORTED — "2 billones 270 mil millones de pesos (8.0% del PIB)" |
| ISR grew **11% real YoY** — highest since 2016 | Block 4, ¶13 | Official assertion | ✅ SUPPORTED — "con una tasa anual de 11%" |
| IVA (VAT) reached **MXN 1,222 billion; 4.3% of GDP**, above historical average of 3.9% | Block 4, ¶14 | Observed fact; consumption-driven interpretation not independently verified | ✅ SUPPORTED — "1 billón 222 mil millones de pesos... el 4.3%, nivel superior a su promedio histórico de 3.9%" |

| Claim | Locator | Category | Verification |
|---|---|---|---|
| Public spending grew **4.1% real YoY**, reaching **MXN 7,569 billion (26.5% of GDP)** | Block 5, ¶15 | Observed fact; growth rate subject to composition effects | ✅ SUPPORTED — "incrementó en un 4.1% real anual, alcanzando los 7 billones 569 mil millones de pesos (26.5% del PIB)" |
| Social protection spending grew **8.7% real**, **5.3% of GDP** — historical maximum | Block 5, ¶16 | Official assertion — definition of "social protection" scope not provided | ✅ SUPPORTED — "incrementó en 8.7% real... se ubican en 5.3%... un nuevo máximo histórico" |
| Physical investment grew **25.2%** (highest since 2009), reaching **3.3% of GDP** — highest since 2016 | Block 5, ¶17 | Official assertion — execution quality, project selection, and any reclassifications not examined | ✅ SUPPORTED — "registró el crecimiento más alto desde el 2009 con una tasa de 25.2%... alcanzó un nivel de 3.3% del PIB, su nivel más alto desde 2016" |
| Transfers to states and municipalities grew **7.3% real YoY** — historical maximum | Block 5, ¶18 | Official assertion — not cross-checked against SHCP treasury data | ✅ SUPPORTED — "alcanzaron el monto más grande desde que se tiene registro con un crecimiento real anual de 7.3%" |
| Primary balance: **deficit of 0.5% of GDP** | Block 5, ¶19 | Observed fact | ✅ SUPPORTED — "el balance primario presentó un déficit de 0.5%" |

| Public Sector Financial Requirements (RFSP): **4.4% of GDP** | Block 5, ¶19 | Observed fact — quasi-fiscal items and contingent liabilities not broken out | ✅ SUPPORTED — "los Requerimientos Financieros del Sector Público se ubican en 4.4%" |

## §6 — Economic Context (macro backdrop)

| Claim | Locator | Category | Verification |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mexico GDP grew **2.9% cumulative to November 2022** | Block 2, ¶5 | Official assertion — 12-month figure incomplete; NSA vs. SA not distinguished | ✅ SUPPORTED — "acumular un crecimiento de 2.9% a noviembre" |
| Unemployment: **2.8% national total; 2.5% for women** — lowest in 17 years | Block 2, ¶5 | Official assertion — definition (strict/broad) not given; underemployment not addressed | ✅ SUPPORTED — "tasas de desempleo más bajas en 17 años: 2.8% en el total y 2.5% para las mujeres" |
| **2.4 million jobs created in 2022**, mostly formal | Block 2, ¶5 | Official assertion — ILO/INEGI cross-check not present | ✅ SUPPORTED — "creación de 2.4 millones de plazas de trabajo en 2022, en su mayoría formales" |
| Private consumption grew **7.1% to October 2022**, more than double historical average | Block 2, ¶6 | Official assertion — partial-year figure; services vs. goods split not given | ✅ SUPPORTED — "consumo privado acumuló hasta octubre de 2022 un crecimiento de 7.1%, tasa superior en más del doble a su promedio histórico" |
| Foreign direct investment (IED): **USD 32 billion to Q3 2022** — highest since 2013 | Block 3, ¶7 | Official assertion — Q3 cumulative; annual figure differs in same document (see block 3) | ✅ SUPPORTED — "flujo de inversión extranjera directa (IED) fuera de 32 mil millones de dólares, nivel no visto desde 2013" |
| Fixed investment grew **5.5% YoY to October**; machinery & equipment: **+12.2%** | Block 3, ¶8 | Official assertion — partial year | ✅ SUPPORTED — "acumuló un crecimiento anual de 5.5% a octubre... el alza de 12.2% anual para maquinaria y equipo" |
| 753,000 new IMSS-insured jobs in 2022; **third highest since 1997** | Block 3, ¶10 | Official assertion — scope limited to IMSS-registered formal employment | ✅ SUPPORTED — "se registraron 753 mil nuevas plazas ante el IMSS... la tercera más alta desde 1997" |
| Real average wage grew **2.7% annual** | Block 3, ¶10 | Official assertion — average vs. median, sectoral distribution not provided | ✅ SUPPORTED — "incremento al salario promedio real de 2.7% anual" |
| During the administration (Dec 2018–Dec 2022), **1.3 million IMSS jobs created** | Block 3, ¶11 | Official assertion — comparison to Calderón and Fox sexenios in same span | ✅ SUPPORTED — "se han creado 1.3 millones de empleos ante el IMSS... superior a las registradas en los sexenios de Felipe Calderón y Vicente Fox" |

| New FDI investments: **USD 14 billion** (second highest after 2013) | Block 3, ¶12 | Official assertion — partial-year Q3 figure; full-year figure may differ | ✅ SUPPORTED — "las nuevas inversiones registraron el segundo mayor monto después de 2013, de 14 mil millones de dólares" |
| Lower capital outflows of **USD 19 billion** vs. 2021 (Q3 2022) | Block 3, ¶13 | Official assertion — flows attributed to investor confidence; no independent assessment | ✅ SUPPORTED — "menor salida de capitales por 19 mil millones de dólares respecto a 2021" |

## §7 — Limitations and Source-Role Flags

1. **Boundary ambiguity:** "Sector público," "gobierno federal," and "balance público" are used interchangeably without clarifying whether figures refer to central government, general government, or public sector (including PEMEX/CFE quasi-fiscal activity).
2. **Nominal vs. real:** Many growth figures are stated as "real" but the deflator (INPC, implicit GDP deflator) is not identified.
3. **Budget vs. actuals:** The "programmed" baseline is not tied to a specific approved budget version; mid-year re-estimates are not discussed.
4. **Audited vs. preliminary:** No distinction is made between audited results and preliminary close figures.
5. **Contingent liabilities:** Arrears, guarantees, off-budget state enterprises (PEMEX/CFE deficits) are not quantified, though RFSP at 4.4% suggests they are partially captured.
6. **Debt definition:** Gross vs. net debt not specified; domestic vs. external split not provided in extract.
7. **Self-reportage:** As an executive-official press release, all claims are self-attributed; no independent audit institution (ASF — Auditoría Superior de la Federación) is cited.
8. **Causality language:** Phrases like "este resultado fue posible por…" attribute outcomes to policy when external factors (oil prices, US demand, remittances) are dominant drivers.
9. **Forward-looking statements:** Projections for 2023 growth and debt pressures are presented without probability ranges or scenario analysis.
10. **Cross-currency:** Some comparisons use USD, some MXN; exchange-rate assumptions are not stated.

---

## REOPEN REQUESTS

1. **Internal inconsistency — unemployment rate:** Block 2 (¶5) reports unemployment rates of 2.8% national and 2.5% for women ("las tasas de desempleo más bajas en 17 años"), while Block 3 (¶10) reports the 2022 *average* unemployment rate was 3.3% ("la tasa de desempleo promedio del año fue de las más bajas desde que se tiene registro"). These are not directly contradictory (point-in-time vs. annual average, different definitions), but the source map should flag this as requiring clarification. The extract does not reconcile the two figures.

2. **Internal inconsistency — employment scope:** Block 2 (¶5) states "2.4 millones de plazas de trabajo en 2022, en su mayoría formales" while Block 3 (¶10) specifies "753 mil nuevas plazas ante el IMSS... principalmente de carácter permanente." The relationship between the broader 2.4 million figure and the narrower 753,000 IMSS-registered figure is unexplained in the extract.

3. **Internal inconsistency — FDI figures:** Block 3 (¶7) reports total IED of "32 mil millones de dólares" while the same block at ¶12 reports "nuevas inversiones registradas... de 14 mil millones de dólares." The extract does not explain what portion of the $32B total flows represents new investment vs. reinvested earnings or inter-company loans, nor why new investments are reported as Q3 partial-year figures while total IED is also Q3.

4. **Block 5 locator correction — debt sustainability claim:** The claim "Debt is sustainable and lower than 2021" was mapped to "Block 5, ¶14" in the draft but the text appears at Block 5, ¶20. The paragraph numbering within Block 5 in the draft does not correspond to the extracted block structure; the corrected locator is Block 5, ¶20.
